steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Your rhythm's a little uneven here.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: The keys are pretty heavy. You're having a hard time once the tempo picks up, aren't you?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: A little, but I think I can manage.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I just need more practice.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: You've gotten plenty of practice today. Your form is starting to slip a bit. If you keep practicing like that, it's going to affect the way you play for the worse.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Take a break. You've already shown lots of improvement.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: But we aren't even sure when our next lesson will be.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I just want to be as good at the piano as you one day!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: You have a gift for this. That day will come in due course.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Yo, Earthspirit!

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: The Doctor sent me...

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Hm? Hey, Eyjafjalla's here too!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I'm teaching Adele how to play the piano.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: And here I thought that's like some specialty skill you were trying to keep to yourself.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I see no need to do that.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Leithanien's packed with music schools, but even they don't force every last person there to study music.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Besides, this is Rhodes Island. It doesn't matter if we don't know how to play any instruments, no?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Most of the entertainment facilities here aren't really to us Leithanians' tastes. Learning how to play an instrument is both a leisure pastime and a good way to enjoy this moment of respite in our hectic lives.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Besides, in Leithanien, you are considered highly educated if you are trained in music, and this isn't something easy to achieve for the Infected in their ghettoes.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: (If she learns how to play music, it will be easier for her to hide her status as an Infected when she leaves for Leithanien in the future.)

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: (I'm not even sure what Earthspirit is talking about anymore!)

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Haha, that tickles! I got it! I got it!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I'm teaching Adele as a kind of experiment. This is to make it easier for me to schedule lessons when I take in other students in the future.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Eyjafjalla's really picking it up quickly, though.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: When was the last time I was here again? It wasn't that long ago, right?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: And now she's playing like a real musician.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: This is only our third lesson. It's still rather choppy, but she can already play the Gaulish piece, 'Moonlight.'

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Even I am jealous of her. I didn't expect Adele to be this talented in music either.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It is things like these beautiful melodies that tell us how wonderful life can be even with what little time we have left.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I think music is really fun. My parents taught me how to play an instrument before, too, but it was a different kind of Leithanian instrument.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: The keys on this piano are so heavy, though! I just can't keep up once the tempo picks up.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: This instrument sounds so nice. It has a really different sound compared to the traditional pianos.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: It's really quite shocking every time I hear its sound.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Provence, hear this! This instrument was actually really huge.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I've never played it, but I saw it at the assembly hall of the school where my mother used to be a teacher.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: It was so big, it stretched the entire length of its walls!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: This particular one is modified from a traditional piano.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: There are actually quite a few compromises made to both reproduce the original's sound and to reduce its size. That is also the reason why the keys are so heavy.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: You are in for a surprise when you hear the real thing.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: So does that mean you will take me to your hometown one of these days?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Looking forward to it!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: My hometown is just a small village in the countryside. You won't find a piano there.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Oh, yeah! I almost forgot.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: The Doctor asked me to come find you. Wanted me to hand this to you.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Oh? Sounds like trouble is coming my way again.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: What is this...? Another geological survey report to be filled out?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Let's see. Hmm... A survey of the soil on the course that Rhodes Island is taking... as well as a Catastrophe forecast report for the surrounding areas...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Analyses of five different soil samples, and each of them requires carbon dating and analyses of their mineral composition.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Did the Doctor say when we'll need this by?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: The day after tomorrow.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: That soon?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Even with a team of three professional geologists, you'd need at least two days to handle this much work.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: And we don't have that many geologists at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Besides, this pharmaceutical company does not have a geological lab, nor are there any plans to add one.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: In conclusion, we are severely lacking in both manpower and facilities, and this is going to continue for the foreseeable future.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Earthspirit, I can help!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: You don't need to worry, Adele.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I'm on the job, so nothing will go wrong. You should take it easy and get some rest. Leave it to me.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I've already gotten plenty of rest today!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Don't you have a field operation with Barty in two days? Just get some rest. I can take care of my own work.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: But I'm afraid I won't be coming with you this time. How is your hearing aid? Is it working fine?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: It's working well in Rhodes Island's indoor environment.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: And I'm hoping there won't be any issues outside either.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Very well. If you need any equipment help for your field op, perhaps you should ask your professor.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: That jackass may be a workaholic, but is nonetheless a caring person.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Hmm... but Professor {@nickname} seems pretty busy lately. I wouldn't want to add to that burden.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: But it's okay, I'll have everything sorted out before I leave.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Yeah, I'm planning on getting a good sleep in today to rest up before starting on the work tomorrow myself.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: I thought you didn't have enough manpower. Are you sure you'll have enough time?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: You need enough rest and adequate entertainment to make sure you can give it your hundred percent while you are on the job.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: And that is especially true for research work. When you are mentally exhausted, you could pull multiple all-nighters and still not be able to solve problems that otherwise would only have taken half an hour.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: That said, I'll have to work overtime for this job. As for my pay...

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: The Doctor said the standard overtime pay will apply.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Very well. As long as there isn't any more work to take care of, I should be able to handle everything.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Perfect, then, I have a report right here!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Hehe, take care of it for me, please? I mean, you're already working overtime anyway.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: What is it this time?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Just the usual.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Geological analysis for my Messenger work.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Where are the samples?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: In your sample box!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: And when do you need it?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: ASAP!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: That's easy for you to say...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: As a Messenger, you don't spend that much time on the Rhodes Island landship to start with.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Every time you're back, you push all your work off on me.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Have you forgotten that we're friends before we're coworkers?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Well, what am I supposed to do? That's how Messenger work is.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Just like right now. I'm only stopping by for a moment.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: You're leaving already?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Yeah, I'm not done with work yet. I'm back just for that report. As soon as I have it, I'm outta here.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Any requirements?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Make sure that whoever reads it has no idea what it's trying to say, to the point they give up on trying to understand it.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Professionally written, then. No problem.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Why don't you want anyone to be able to read it?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: This is just a kind of report for us Messengers, though it's not usually us who get to read it.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Most of the time, it's for our employers or the people in charge of the place.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Catastrophe Messengers sometimes hand scientists data for their analysis, and then they will decide with the data whether there's a need to move somewhere else to avoid Catastrophes. That's one of the many ways we work.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: By doing that, we transfer the risk of a forecast being incorrect to the person making the call.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: That way, if it turns out there isn't a Catastrophe, the economic impact of the city's resettlement isn't on the Messenger's head.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Catastrophe Messengers are humans after all, and when you possess all the emotions that humans normally have, mistakes are inevitable.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: You hear of Messengers who lose confidence, start doubting themselves after an incorrect forecast, and they ultimately leave the business altogether.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It's only natural for us to make mistakes, but the consequences that Catastrophe Messengers face for their mistakes are far too severe...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: This method of shifting blame was created to protect the Messengers.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Of course, that also gave us more data analysis work.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It takes time for them to come and go as well, so the only Messengers that I can help are the ones in Rhodes Island's surroundings.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: That's not too bad. It gives you more time at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: If you still ran all over the world as both a Catastrophe Messenger and a geologist like before, we probably wouldn't even get to meet once a year.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Is that why you waste every single chance we get to meet?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Ehe?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Stop it with the happy smiley face!

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: You were the one who told me to do that!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: That's right. I just don't want anyone to repeat Professor Bachmann's tragedy.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Oh, is that the famous Professor Bachmann from the Gurk Private Academy? She's a famed geologist and musician in Leithanien. So she was your mentor!

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: My mother knew her.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: When I was young, she came to my house once during a birthday party.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Of course, she didn't know it was my birthday. She only stopped by to ask my mom about work.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: But once she found out it was my birthday, she played a piece for me.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I can still remember that beautiful melody.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: She's the person whom I look up to the most.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Did something happen to Professor Bachmann?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: A noble from the countryside appointed her as their Catastrophe Messenger, and she gave them a professional analysis.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Professor Bachmann used to be a Catastrophe Messenger?!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: She is of course more well known as a geologist and a musician, but she was indeed a Catastrophe Messenger.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: The noble asked Professor Bachmann to give them a final, explicit answer—whether a Catastrophe was going to happen...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: ...and whether the citizens would need to move.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Professor Bachmann was actually a very simple-minded Leithanian scholar. She was old, but she was not a very shrewd person.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: She always chose the most conservative of methods. That's also why, after she conducted an analysis of the area's geological samples, she recommended that the citizens leave right away.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: In the end, the Catastrophe didn't happen.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: The citizens went back to where they were, and their crops were ruined.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: They had to give what little food they had left to the nobles and starve.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: When the commoners handed over their food in tears, this is what the nobles told them...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: 'This is all Bachmann's fault. If her predictions weren't off, we would never have evacuated.'

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: 'It's all her fault that you have to go through this.'

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: 'This is all her fault.'

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: That ignited the commoners' ire.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Professor Bachmann was attacked that very same night. They bashed her head with a rock, then tied her up and burned her to death.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Not Professor Bachmann...!

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: You don't want that to happen to anyone else.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: You want to protect others with knowledge, not violence.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Is the reason you like geology so much because you can use this knowledge to protect others?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: No, not exactly.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: My motivation is actually very simple. Unlike you, I wasn't very talented in Arts.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I have gotten better at Originium Arts after my infection, but that doesn't mean I've come to have a talent for it.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I just don't have a knack for Originium Arts. I'm too clumsy.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: You are too humble, you know? If you're supposed to be clumsy, then I guess I'm probably the stupidest person there is.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: You got the last part right at least.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Considering my talent, forcing myself to learn Originium Arts wouldn't get me anywhere.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I was smart when I was a kid, and my parents had high hopes for me.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I read lots of books. I was mastering certain basic Arts and their associated theories much earlier than normal.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Everyone thought I was primed to do great things. My parents hoped that I would elevate our family's status, which would give us the opportunity to move to the city.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: But as I grew up and the things that I had to learn became more complicated, I found out I wasn't going to get anywhere with just my 'smarts.'

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Even though I knew the theories like the back of my hand, I just simply didn't have the talent. I had no way to do the things I couldn't do.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Geology is different. This is where I could find myself as long as I studied hard.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: This is where I can find that me my parents were hoping for me to be.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: So, from the get-go, you pretty much had no choice but to study geology?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: No, I wouldn't say that, but it was Professor Bachmann and her geology lessons that rescued and accepted me when I hit the rock bottom of my depression.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It was only from that point onward that I started to study geology, and through each small achievement I made, I learned to love it.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: This is the place where I belong. This is my home.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Geology sounds pretty boring, though.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Quite the contrary. Even if you stack all the books in the world together, the stack will only go so tall.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: But geology is an endless bookshelf.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Each and every field study will get you a different story and help you understand the history of that place.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Just like they are whispering to me...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Geology is a natural library that has no limits.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: From that point of view, it's not boring, and it certainly doesn't make me feel lonely.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: So you think it's pretty fun working here?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: No, Provence. Running tests and doing research inside a lab aren't geology.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Analyzing the contents of soil samples brought back by Messengers and estimating the chances of a Catastrophe happening isn't really geology either.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: The equipment that Earthspirit is using is portable, and its functions are simple. It's meant to be used when she's taking samples outdoors.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I've been staying inside with my equipment because Rhodes Island and our Catastrophe Messengers need me.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Although it does feel like I've had a little too much on my plate lately. Why is it that even the Messengers I barely know are here asking me for reports?

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Well, as a Messenger, it really drags me down if I make a bad prediction.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Your reports help us make a general projection.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: These reports are supposed to be written by researchers on the subject, but even though their work may be professional, they also add lots of stuff that has nothing to do with our work.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: But not only are you an excellent geologist, you're a great Messenger yourself.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: So even...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Even if you didn't need to show your employers any reports, you still wanted one to use as a reference.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Oh? No wonder I've had so much more work lately. So this is why.

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Heheh, thanks to me, you are like a legend among Catastrophe Messengers!

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: 'The Master of Fraktur.' That's what they call you. Doesn't that sound super cool?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: So all those times you had me do your work...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: All that overtime...

steps.name: Provence
steps.text: Oh, right, I gotta take a shower now. I'll leave the documents here—

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Stop right there!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Oh no, my legs are going numb.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I'll hunt her down for you, Earthspirit!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: No, no need. It'll get better after I take a few steps! You should get some rest!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: My leg... ugh... that hurts...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Provence, hold it right there!
